plain: The Tunguska event, the huge blast over Siberia on 30 June 1908, was an air burst from an object belonging to the Taurid stream, a band of meteor debris Earth passes through each year, according to the researcher Randall Carlson. Carlson tells this on two episodes without naming a source, once in his own interview and once in an episode with the writer Graham Hancock, where the record credits it to Hancock. If true, it would make Tunguska one piece of a recurring cosmic hazard rather than a one-off.
